title: Normalized evaluation over one algebraically closed field
statement: Let E be a totally disconnected normed field and Omega an algebraically closed field in the same universe. Fix z in Spec Omega. There exists an additive finite-colimit-preserving functor H from internal modules over the condensed E coefficient ring on Spec Omega to E-vector spaces. Its regular module admits E-linear coordinates b identifying H(f) with multiplication by the value at z of the continuous coefficient obtained by conjugating f with the specified canonical continuous realization and applying it to 1.

proof.text: Equip presheaf evaluation with its pointwise strong monoidal structure, with identity unit and tensor comparisons. Compose it with the lax monoidal sheaf-to-presheaf functor to obtain final-object abelian sections F on Spec Omega. The theorem geometric_field_proetale_evaluation_exact supplies finite-colimit preservation of F. The source-library mapMod and comap functors transport internal modules and compute their underlying groups and maps.

Spec Omega is a singleton. The explicit ring isomorphism pointConstants sends a lifted element of E to its constant continuous function, and its inverse evaluates at z. The sheaf multiplication comparison Sheaf.μ_comp_map_mul shows that the induced monoid object on the sections of the continuous coefficient sheaf is precisely its ordinary section-ring monoid object. Compose constants with F applied to the inverse of condensedFieldContinuousMapIso to obtain the monoid isomorphism r : ULift E -> F(A), where A is the condensed coefficient ring. Define H by F.mapMod A, restriction of internal scalars along r, the already constructed internalToModule functor from the internal-module/ordinary-module equivalence, and restriction from ULift E to E.

The inverse of r identifies the internally evaluated regular module with the regular ULift E module: its linearity is the multiplicativity equation for inv r, with r followed by inv r cancelled. Map this module isomorphism through internalToModule and restriction of scalars, and compose with ULift.down to get E-linear coordinates b. Thus b is inv r followed by ULift.down, and b.symm sends a to r(ULift.up a). Expand inv r as the evaluated continuous realization followed by evaluation at z. Applied to H(f) and b.symm(1), this is exactly the definition of condensedFieldPointCoefficient. All four factors of H are additive. F.mapMod preserves finite colimits because F does, internal restriction of scalars computes colimits, internalToModule is an equivalence, and ordinary restriction of scalars preserves finite colimits. This gives all three conjuncts of the claimed existence theorem.

proof_origin.note: C4 implements the existing evaluation plan without further split-offs. The normalization uses the specified continuous realization, not an arbitrary coefficient-ring isomorphism.

theorem exists_condensedField_point_evaluation
    (E : Type u) [NormedField E] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace E]
    (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (z : Spec (.of Ω)) :
    ∃ H : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology (Spec (.of Ω))) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
        (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousCoefficientRingObj E) (Spec (.of Ω))) ⥤
        ModuleCat.{u + 1} E,
      H.Additive ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits H ∧ CondensedFieldPointScalarProperty E Ω z H
